question: Which structure of the eye is responsible for the greatest amount of light refraction?
explanation: The cornea provides the primary refractive power of the eye due to its curved shape and the air-tissue interface. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the main job of the lens in the eye during normal vision?

options.A: Producing the fluid that nourishes the front of the eye
options.B: Turning light waves into electrical nerve signals
options.C: Controlling the total amount of light entering the eye
options.D: Fine-tuning the focus of incoming light onto the retina

explanation: The lens changes shape to adjust focus for near and distant objects after the cornea does the initial light bending. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h1)

question: What happens to the pupil when you walk from a dark room into bright sunlight?

options.A: It gets bigger to catch more light
options.B: It pushes forward to help focus
options.C: It flattens to reduce light bending
options.D: It gets smaller to let less light in

explanation: The pupil constricts in bright light to protect the sensitive cells inside the retina from being overloaded. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h2)

question: What happens inside the eye when you look at something very close to you?

options.A: Supporting fibers pull the lens flat
options.B: The iris opens up wide to let in more light
options.C: Ciliary muscles relax and the lens flattens
options.D: Ciliary muscles contract and the lens thickens

explanation: When the ciliary muscle tightens, the supporting fibers loosen, allowing the natural elasticity of the lens to make it rounder for near vision. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which cells in the retina are mainly responsible for helping us see at night and in dim light?
explanation: Rods contain high amounts of a pigment called rhodopsin, making them very sensitive to low levels of light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h3)

question: What happens inside a rod cell when light hits it?

options.A: Sodium channels open and the cell fires an electric impulse
options.B: Potassium rushes in to reset the resting state
options.C: Sodium channels close and the cell becomes more negative inside
options.D: Chemical release increases to stimulate nearby cells

explanation: When light hits the rod cell, it causes sodium channels to close, leading to a drop in the release of chemical messengers. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve carries visual messages from the retina to the brain?
explanation: The optic nerve, or cranial nerve II, is formed by nerve fibers carrying visual signals away from the eyeball. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h4)

question: What happens to visual nerve fibers as they meet at the optic chiasm?

options.A: Fibers from the outer side of the retina cross over while inner fibers stay straight
options.B: Only the fibers from the left eye cross over to the right side
options.C: Nerve fibers from the inner side of each retina cross over to the opposite side of the brain
options.D: All visual signals stop and mix together before heading to the brain

explanation: This crossing over at the optic chiasm blends signals from both eyes, which is essential for depth perception. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why does it take time for your eyes to adjust when you walk into a very dark room?

options.A: The visual center in the brain needs a long rest
options.B: It takes time for the light-sensitive pigment in rod cells to rebuild
options.C: All the cone cells get tired out at the same time
options.D: The pupil takes a long time to open up

explanation: Dark adaptation relies on the chemical process of rebuilding rhodopsin stores after bright light has used them up. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h5)

question: How is the human eye able to see and distinguish many different colors?

options.A: By constantly changing the fluid inside the eye
options.B: By switching back and forth between rods and cones during the day
options.C: By filtering light through different shapes of the cornea
options.D: By comparing the combined signals from three different types of cone cells

explanation: Color vision depends on red, green, and blue cones working together so the brain can interpret different shades. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h5)
